Hi Sara —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a one-page MAP + benchmarking playbook we propose to execute. High level:

Objective:
- Validate that Redwood can meet Acme's latency & throughput SLOs for your realtime inference workload, and characterize burst vs steady-state behavior so your app can set appropriate client-side limits.

Success criteria (examples we propose; happy to adjust):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): <= 90ms median, <= 180ms p95 for single-turn 256-token prompts
- Latency (generation p50/p95/p99 per-token/response): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 650ms under steady-state
- Sustained throughput: 350 QPS sustained with 100-200ms mean response window (depends on prompt length/sequence)
- Burst handling: tolerate 2x sustained QPS for short windows (1-2s) with graceful queuing and bounded tail latency

Test plan summary:
1) Lab run (Redwood-managed): controlled ramp test to reproduce baseline (0->350 QPS), collect TTFT & tail latency by concurrency slice
2) Burst windows: repeated microbursts (2x, 4x sustained) for 1s/2s/5s to observe queueing and server-side backpressure
3) Steady-state: hold target QPS for 10m windows to validate stability and memory/KV cache behavior
4) Rate-limit tuning: iterate on service-level token batching and burst window (suggested defaults included)
5) Acceptance: validation dataset + pass/fail checklist we agree on

Deliverables & timeline (suggested):
- Lab run + initial results: 2 business days after sign-off
- Tuning pass & rerun: +3 business days
- Final report + MAP update: +1 business day

Please review the attached MAP_Acme_v1.xlsx which contains the exact test inputs and pass/fail thresholds. If you prefer Redwood to run the lab tests against a sandbox account, confirm and we will schedule a 2-hour pilot slot.

Internal note to @Lauren and @Karthik: please review the ETA and suggested tuning knobs in the sheet; I expect a quick lab run early next week.

Thanks —

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: FW: Lab ramp run — preliminary results
Attachments: ramp_results_0802.csv; rate_limit_tuning_notes.md

Neha / Lauren —

I ran the lab ramp yesterday against the model variant we discussed (quantized v2). Summary of preliminary observations (numbers are median unless noted):

Test setup: 4 machines (A100 equiv) behind the Redwood serving runtime, warm KV cache, prompt payload ~320 tokens, gen length 64. We used the MAP thresholds in the sheet.

Key metrics by concurrency slice:
- 50 concurrent sessions: TTFT p50 = 82ms, p95 = 140ms; response latency p50 = 110ms, p95 = 220ms
- 200 concurrent sessions: TTFT p50 = 95ms, p95 = 190ms; response latency p50 = 150ms, p95 = 320ms
- 500 concurrent sessions (approaching queuing): TTFT p50 = 140ms, p95 = 380ms; response latency p50 = 260ms, p95 = 760ms
- 800 concurrent sessions (saturation): sustained throughput flattened ~420 QPS and tail latencies increased; observed server queueing leads to p99 > 1.5s

Burst window tests (2x, 4x sustained for 1s/2s):
- Short bursts (2x for 1s): mostly absorbed with queuing, small p95 bump (~200–300ms)
- Longer/stronger bursts (4x for 2s+): we saw request drops when queuing > 750ms; need client-side retry/backoff or server-side rate-limit shaping

Rate-limit & tuning notes (high level):
- Default service-level token_batch_size = 16 is fine for steady-state; increase to 32 for improved throughput at cost of marginal p50 increase
- Recommend burst_window_ms = 250ms, max_burst_tokens = 800 for Acme's traffic profile to avoid sudden p99 blowups
- Enable KV cache pre-warm for high-concurrency slices (reduces TTFT variability)

Actionables:
- I'll attach the raw ramp_results_0802.csv and a short notes file with the tuning knobs.
- Suggested acceptance: validate two steady-state 10-minute windows at 350 QPS with p95 <= 350ms and p99 <= 900ms.

Risks / caveats:
- If Avro-style payload sizes increase beyond current test prompts, throughput targets will drop ~15–25% without re-quantization.
- If Acme wants sub-200ms p95 at 400+ QPS we should consider a dedicated pool (redwood dedicated) or lower-precision model variant.

Happy to walk through the CSV with Acme SREs.

-Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
